notes.markdown:
# Python Lists

A list is an ordered, mutable collection in Python.

layman.simpleExplanation: Think of a Python list like a flexible shopping basket that can hold multiple items.
layman.analogyOrStory: You can add items, remove items and change existing items in the basket.

example1.content: A list can represent a sequence of items that must be processed in order.

example2.content: A list can represent products selected by a customer.

real_life.title: A Shopping List
real_life.scenario: Imagine writing several products on a shopping list and changing the list while shopping.
real_life.why_it_matters: Programming applications frequently need to store and manipulate collections of related values.

technical.markdown: Python lists are ordered, mutable sequences. They support indexing, slicing and dynamic resizing.

qa_pairs.question: Are Python lists mutable?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes. Existing list elements can be changed after the list is created.

qa_pairs.question: Can a Python list contain different data types?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes. A Python list can contain objects of different types.
